business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan, China (Taiwan as investor-origin sub-state; WFOE incorporated under PRC Company Law in mainland China)

Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and the Straits Exchange Foundation (2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 of 2024, namely the Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information, effective 1 November 2024, together with the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2024 revision), the PRC Company Law (2023 amendment, effective 1 July 2024), and the Regulations on the Administration of the Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746), require all WFOEs to identify, verify, and file beneficial owner information to the government through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the PBOC Integrated Regulatory Data Platform.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Investing Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization track only: notarization by a Taiwan notary public, certification by the competent Taiwan court or MOEA authority, then consular legalization through the PRC representative office or cross-strait notarization verification through SEF/ARATS. Do NOT chain any Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Company Registration Facts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Commercial Registration Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization track only: Taiwan notarization, MOEA or court certification, followed by PRC consular legalization or cross-strait verification. This path is parallel to and mutually exclusive with the Hague Apostille path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE incorporation and appointment of the local legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Parent Company Board of Directors, certified by Taiwan MOEA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization track only: board resolution notarized in Taiwan, certified by competent Taiwan authority, then legalized by PRC consular channel or verified through the SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization mechanism; no Apostille to be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the Taiwan Investing Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Parent Company and Taiwan MOEA certified copy repository
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization track only: certified true copy notarized in Taiwan, verified by MOEA or district court, then consularized/verified for mainland China use; the Hague Apostille path is inapplicable and must not be layered onto this track.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan Parent Company's principal commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank maintaining the corporate account relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization track only: original bank letterhead with wet-ink signature and corporate seal, signature notarized by a Taiwan notary, followed by certification and PRC consular/cross-strait verification; no Hague Apostille may be used or chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, senior managers, and material counterparties against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions lists, and domestic PBOC/SAMR enforcement blacklists. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, immediate family members, and close associates, with enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, continuous transaction monitoring, adverse media and negative news review, and annual risk re-rating for this high-risk licensed virtual card-issuing fintech.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters; the four-tier statutory naming convention is administrative division + distinctive name + industry/operation characteristics + company form. For a WFOE the company form must denote limited liability. Pinyin romanization and an English trade name are permitted only as supplementary transliterations for banking and cross-border marketing; the Chinese legal name is exclusively controlling for governance, tax, and UBO filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Any name rejection will be issued electronically by SAMR with the offending token or classification identified. The applicant must resubmit a corrected name through the same online portal within 5 working days, or apply for an extension no later than 5 working days before the current reservation expires. If the rejection is challenged as unlawful, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR authority within 60 days of receipt, or bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within 6 months. For financial and card-related tokens, a non-objection letter from PBOC or CBIRC must be obtained and attached to the resubmission; the registrar may grant one discretionary 30-day extension.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.authentication track note: Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel, mutually exclusive authentication paths. For Taiwan-origin documents only the Consular Legalization/cross-strait verification track is used; no apostille sequence may be added.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this ISIC 6619 licensed virtual card-issuing fintech. Local tax authorities, SAMR, and all Chinese banks reject virtual-office arrangements because a licensed card-issuing and spend-management entity must maintain a physical office in the registered city, staffed compliance personnel, accessible books and records, onsite IT or data custody, and a visible corporate signboard. A non-residential dedicated physical lease with utility bills in the company name is mandatory before PBOC pre-licensing consultation and corporate bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: original lease contract, recent utility or property-management invoices, site signboard, employee roster and job cards, statutory legal representative presence indicators, original company chops, accounting ledgers, payroll records, AML/CFT compliance manual, and card-operation or IT audit logs. Quantified risk: 80% probability of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax physical inspection within the first 12 months after licensing; 100% probability of a PBOC onsite supervisory visit before card-license approval; risk rises to 95% if a virtual office or commercial mailbox is detected, and banks will refuse corporate account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.alternate_registered_office_note: If the WFOE is registered in a free-trade zone, the physical office lease must be compliant with the zone's operating-substance rules and cannot be substituted with a mailing address or aggregator service.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Republic of China), Articles 1, 2, 6, 8, 128-131, 135, 138-139, 154, 156, 192, 216, 237, 404-408 and related enforcement rules; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 1, 5, 7, 10 and 15; Investment Commission Regulations for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.); Company Registration Cloud online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (Articles of Incorporation) with all statutory certification attachments and capital verification certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Taiwan company limited by shares under the Company Act (minimum capital requirement was abolished in 2009). The foreign investor must, however, remit and deposit the capital amount specified in the Investment Commission approval letter, and the bank must issue a Capital Deposit Certificate as capital verification. No blocked escrow account is required at ordinary incorporation stage. If the company later applies for an FSC Electronic Payment Institution License, the FSC minimum paid-up capital rule (approximately NT$100,000,000 for a comprehensive electronic payment institution, or such lower tier as set for limited functions) must be met and maintained in a designated Taiwanese bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD. (Taiwan), a company limited by shares. Adoption by unanimous written consent of the board of directors in lieu of a formal board meeting. RESOLVED: 1. Capital Subscription and Allotment. That the authorized share capital of this Company is divided into ordinary shares with a par value of NT$10 per share, and that the total paid-up capital has been fully subscribed by the sole shareholder in cash pursuant to the incorporation plan and the Investment Commission approval. The board confirms that all approved foreign-invested capital has been lawfully remitted and deposited into the Company preparatory bank account, and the bank capital verification certificate has been issued. The board further approves the issuance of share certificates, the registration of the shareholder register, and the filing of the required share issuance report with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 2. Banking Arrangements. That the principal operating bank accounts of the Company be established with the designated authorized bank in Taiwan, and that any two of the Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, or authorized director be jointly empowered to open, maintain, sign, operate, and close such accounts, including authority to draw checks, wire funds, execute foreign exchange transactions, enter into online banking agreements, and issue bank mandates on behalf of the Company. 3. Registered Office. That the registered office and principal place of business of the Company be fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, which shall be the statutory address for official correspondence, service of process, and all government filings, and that the lease and facility documents previously reviewed by the board are hereby ratified. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. That the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer, Corporate Secretary, and External Supervisor. Each officer shall serve in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act and the Company Articles, and the board may fix compensation and emoluments from time to time. The board also authorizes the Corporate Secretary and the Managing Director to sign all incorporation, tax, and financial licensing instruments, and to engage counsel for statutory filings. This resolution shall be effective immediately and continue until revoked by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval and Reserve the Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.) and MOEA Company Registration Cloud
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application to the Investment Commission for a foreign investment approval under the Foreign Investment Act. The application must include the proposed Taiwan company English and Chinese names, scope of business, shareholder structure, paid-up capital, bank references, and a five-year business plan. Concurrently reserve the proposed company name through the MOEA Company Registration Cloud system. Because the entity is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the Investment Commission must verify that the business activity does not appear on the Negative List for investment and that the investor meets source-of-funds and beneficial ownership checks. The approval letter will authorize the foreign exchange remittance and the subsequent company registration. After approval, the name reservation is automatically linked to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of the foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing local representative
Five-year business plan and financial projections
Bank reference letters and proof of source of funds
Completed AML KYC beneficial ownership declaration
Company name reservation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or suspends review, provide supplementary documents within 14 days via the online portal. If the investment is partially disallowed, amend the business scope and capital plan and resubmit. If formally rejected, file a written administrative appeal to the MOEA Investment Commission within 30 days from the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Remit Capital, Open Preparatory Bank Account, and Obtain Capital Verification Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan; Central Bank of Taiwan (foreign exchange reporting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission approval, open a temporary pre-incorporation bank account at an authorized bank in the name of the company preparatory office. Instruct the foreign investor to remit the approved paid-up capital from overseas in foreign currency or New Taiwan Dollars, and direct the bank to convert and deposit the funds into the temporary account. The bank then issues a Capital Deposit Certificate showing the deposit date, amount, and account number, which serves as capital verification for company registration. The bank will report the direct investment remittance to the Central Bank in accordance with foreign exchange regulations. Maintain accurate records of the incoming remittance, conversion rates, and any bank charges. This step is mandatory before filing the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Pre-incorporation bank account application
Company name reservation certificate
Foreign investor remittance instruction
Corporate resolution and power of attorney for opening account
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends remittance for AML or KYC reasons, submit a source-of-funds statement and corroborating financial documents. If the Central Bank flags the transaction, apply for a foreign exchange approval. Correct any currency type discrepancy or account name mismatch before the capital certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Officer Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public or licensed attorney; company formation counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese with a certified English counterpart, containing the company name, registered office, authorized and paid-up share capital, classes of shares, board composition, supervisor, corporate governance rules, and financial year. Each promoter, director, and supervisor must sign the Articles and affix their seal. If required by the investor, have the documents notarized by a Taiwan notary to satisfy foreign due diligence. Prepare the written consent or board resolution for directors and supervisor to assume office, along with a statement that none is disqualified under the Taiwan Company Act. These documents are then submitted to the MOEA as part of the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Promoters or incorporators signatures
Directors and supervisor consent letters
ID or passport copies of each director and supervisor
Power of attorney for legal counsel
Notarization certificates if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registrar objects to defective signatures or missing authority, cure by obtaining corrected signatures or a fresh power of attorney from the foreign investor. If a proposed director fails eligibility, replace the director and amend the consent list before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration with the MOEA Department of Commercial Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; Company Registration Cloud online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Company Registration Cloud portal with government ID and electronic signature. Complete the Application for Company Registration using the reserved company name. Attach the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, Investment Commission approval, consent letters, directors and supervisor identity documents, registered office lease, and the company seal specimen. Pay the required filing fee. The MOEA reviews the incorporation record against the Company Act and, upon approval, issues the Company Registration Certificate and a unified business tax identification number. This registration makes the company a lawful legal person with capacity to open formal bank accounts, execute contracts, and apply for the required financial licenses.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Registration Application Form
Approved Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Investment Commission approval letter
Directors and supervisor consent letters and ID copies
Registered office lease and landlords consent
Company seal and specimen signature card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA queries the filing, use the portal to submit supplementary explanations or amended dossiers within 10 days. If the registration is refused, correct the defect and refile, or pursue an administrative appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days from the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax Registration and Apply for the Financial Supervisory Commission License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance for tax registration; Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau for virtual card issuance license; Municipal Fire and Labor authorities for office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After MOEA registration, register the company for business tax and uniform invoice issuance at the local National Taxation Bureau and obtain the business registration certificate. For the financial license, submit the FSC application for an Electronic Payment Institution License or the applicable virtual card issuance approval, including business plan, AML and CFT internal controls, systems and program specifications, capital adequacy certificate, contracts with a licensed settlement bank and card network such as Mastercard or Visa Direct, outsourcing contracts, director and supervisor background checks, and financial projections. Because the operation is office-based and not manufacturing, no Environmental Impact Assessment is required. For the office, obtain the fire safety inspection certificate and register for labor and health insurance.
required_dossiers: Tax registration application and uniform invoice registration form
Company Registration Certificate
FSC license application form
AML and CFT program and policies
Card network and bank partner agreements
Proof of paid-up or minimum capital
Business plan and internal audit charter
Fire safety inspection report
Occupational safety registration
Lease agreement and building use certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, correct the address and director data before the 10-day notice. If the FSC returns a deficiency letter, respond with supplemental internal control opinions within the 30-day cure period. If the license is denied, appeal to the FSC Appeals Committee under due process, or restructure the operation as a software service provider to a licensed bank and apply for a more limited registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Banking Bureau; supported by the MOEA Investment Commission for foreign investment business scope approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Payment Institution License / Virtual Card Issuer Approval (FSC-granted) under the Act on Electronic Payment Institutions; in addition, Mastercard and Visa Direct program approvals are required for network access

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based financial intermediary operation (ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320); no EIA registration or full EIA report required under the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act Annex
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. No industrial wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste are generated. Office wastewater discharges to the public sewer system are subject to municipal BOD and SS limits. Any electronic waste, batteries, or IT equipment must be handled under the EPA Resource Recycling Act and related regulations. If a data center or server farm is added later, refrigerant emissions and green IT requirements will apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate from the Municipal Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, a Building Occupancy and Structural Safe Use Certificate from the Municipal Public Works Office, and a General Occupational Safety registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. No civil defense permit for explosive, chemical, or hazardous industrial storage is required for this virtual card issuing and spend management business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), operating through the National Taxation Bureaus in the Taipei, Kaohsiung, Northern, Central, and Southern districts; electronic filing and registration portal: Taiwan Tax Internet Filing and Payment Service (tax.nat.gov.tw) and the E-Invoice Turnkey Network maintained by the Ministry of Finance Financial Information Service Company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned limited company (Taiwan WFOE) or the Taiwan branch of a foreign enterprise must first complete company or branch incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA). After incorporation, the entity must file Business Tax Registration with the local National Taxation Bureau before commencing business. The Bureau issues a Taxpayer Identification Code known as the 8-digit Unified Business Number (UBIN), which serves as the TIN for business tax, corporate income tax, customs, and Uniform Invoice purposes. For a non-resident entity without a fixed place of business in Taiwan, a qualified fiscal agent or tax representative must be appointed under power of attorney to apply for a non-resident tax ID and handle tax declarations. Standard filings include the registration application, MOEA incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, investment approval or foreign investment permit, identity documents of shareholders and directors, and proof of a Taiwan registered office. There is no minimum capital requirement, but the virtual card issuing business requires a special license from the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) before tax registration because the activity is classified as a high-risk special license in the payment cards sector.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or a hybrid mismatch election. Business and corporate income tax classification follows the Taiwan Company Act and the Income Tax Act, with no elective pass-through treatment for a limited company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (VAT) under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: New Taiwan Dollars (TWD): mandatory registration is required if average monthly turnover exceeds NT$80,000 from the sale of goods or NT$40,000 from services. A licensed virtual card issuing entity is registrable from day one because it holds a statutory financial services license and issues Uniform Invoices, even if below the general small-business threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue Uniform Invoices. Businesses meeting the electronic invoicing criteria are required to use the E-Invoice (Electronic Uniform Invoice) system and upload invoice data through the Ministry of Finance Turnkey Network using the XML/API protocol within 48 hours of issuance. The system assigns an encrypted invoice number and a random check code to each B2C transaction, enabling instant online validation and anti-fraud risk scoring. B2B E-Invoices are exchanged through the same turnkey network without a physical fiscal stamp, but the near-real-time transmission and response message from the Ministry of Finance integration platform constitute the electronic fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, a 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported from Taiwan if the goods are actually cleared through Customs and leave the territory, and to services rendered to overseas clients where the service is strictly used outside Taiwan and the remuneration for the service is received from abroad. The exporter must maintain a complete audit trail demonstrating physical export, supply of qualifying services, and receipt of foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) certified by Taiwan Customs
Ocean or Air Bill of Lading showing Taiwan as the port of export and a foreign consignee
Sales contract or service agreement with the overseas counterparty
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued foreign exchange receipt voucher showing the foreign payment
Financial institution custodian records proving export payment collection, if the export is settled through a factoring or card network
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited against customs exit records, bank foreign exchange receipts, and the financial institution's electronic transaction logs. If the exporter fails to repatriate foreign currency proceeds within the statutory 180-day period or cannot substantiate the customs declaration and banking records, the 0% rate is rescinded. The underpaid 5% business tax is retrospectively assessed together with late payment interest and a delinquency penalty. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, fraudulent or intentionally deceptive zero-rating can attract a penalty of up to five times the evaded tax and criminal liability under the Tax Collection Act for the responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, acting under the authority of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi is partially convertible. Current account transactions, including cross-border service fees related to virtual card programme management, licence fees to Mastercard or Visa, and merchant payout fees, are generally convertible after the designated bank performs documentary genuineness checks and reports through SAFE's foreign exchange monitoring system. Capital account items remain heavily regulated. Inbound equity capital from the Taiwan shareholder requires FDI registration with the relevant commerce authority and SAFE, a dedicated foreign-currency capital account, and post-injection conversion subject to the negative list. Outbound dividend remittances require audited financial statements, completed corporate income tax and withholding tax settlements, and SAFE-compliant bank verification; they are not subject to routine approval but will be suspended if the bank identifies irregular cross-strait flows or unresolved tax filings. Export receipts and service fees must be repatriated to China, but enterprises may retain foreign currency in designated operating accounts or sell it to a bank at the market rate; no compulsory conversion ratio exists. Profit remittance hurdles include demonstrating that the RMB profit is from genuine business, documenting the board resolution, and matching the remittance with prior tax payment records. Taiwan-related remittances are treated as cross-border flows requiring the same underlying documentation and are monitored through cross-strait financial channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to a PRC-designated foreign-exchange account through an authorised bank and reconciled with customs export declarations via SAFE's trade monitoring system within 180 days of the customs declaration date; delays require a documented SAFE deferral record. The mandatory conversion ratio is nil: China has abolished forced surrender, so the WFOE may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or convert any portion into RMB at prevailing market rates. For service-trade income, including virtual card fees, the same 180-day receipt verification logic applies using contracts, invoices, and bank receipts; the A/B/C classification of the entity determines the pre-verification intensity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI Registered Capital / Basic Operational Currency Account
Cross-Border Capital Settlement Account / Basic Operational RMB Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Designated Foreign-Exchange Capital Account / Renminbi Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary banking relationship. A Chinese WFOE engaged in PBOC-supervised virtual card issuing must safeguard customer funds in licensed domestic banking institutions; offshore digital EMIs generally lack a PBOC payment institution license and cannot offer RMB accounts, CNAPS/CIPS participation, or clearing via domestic card networks. They cannot legally replace the domestic bank for capital escrow, tax withholding, or SAFE submission. Offshore EMIs may only be used as ancillary international payment gateways for non-RMB traffic under a licensed sponsor and must sweep balances through the domestic Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance of the statutory legal representative is generally mandatory for opening the bank account, especially for high-risk PBOC-licensed payment businesses. Remote video KYC may be used for replenishment but not to replace the first meeting. A Taiwanese resident legal representative who cannot travel to mainland must execute a notarised power of attorney in Taiwan authenticated by the Cross-Strait Notarization and Verification mechanism; even then, most Tier-1 banks require the representative to appear once for a face-to-face risk interview. Remote consular proxy opening without physical in-branch visit is not accepted for capital escrow accounts; for secondary operating accounts, after the UBO register and risk assessment, some banks permit a notarised proxy to complete administrative formalities, but beneficial owner interviews remain compulsory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity across the Taiwan-resident parent chain, particularly nominee arrangements or multi-layer offshore holding entities, with insufficient source of wealth for the ultimate human owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full constitutional ownership chain to natural persons; UBO register; notarised Taiwan identification documents; source of wealth package comprising three years of audited financial statements, tax returns, personal bank statements, investment or asset purchase certificates, and inheritance or gift records; Cross-Strait authentication letters; signed declaration confirming no undisclosed nominees; board-approved corporate governance chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model is risk-classified as high-risk special-license payment services under ISIC 6619 and NAICS 522320, with possible exposure to unlicensed deposit-taking or card-scheme compliance failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PBOC Payment Business License or valid sponsorship agreement with a licensed bank; Mastercard and Visa programme membership certificates; AML/CFT programme with a designated compliance officer; sanctions screening and transaction monitoring policy documents; external audit opinion on compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering Law and the Administrative Measures for Non-Financial Payment Institutions; customer-funds safeguarding attestation showing no commingling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows to and from Taiwan showing mismatch between virtual-card customer spend and underlying merchant contracts, creating a possible channel for unexplained fund transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with customers and merchants; commercial fund-flow diagrams; historical transaction records with merchant category codes; invoices, purchase orders, and delivery confirmations; customer KYB and KYC files; treasury policy on SAFE purpose-code classification; audit report on one-to-one matching of card loads and spend files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions exposure, or questionable end-use of payment services, especially because Chinese banks screen for politically exposed persons and restricted end-users in cross-strait relationships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party negative-news and reputational-risk screening reports; sanctions and PEP screening results for all beneficial owners and directors; compliance certification from card networks; end-use attestations from corporate customers; legal opinion on export-control and dual-use classification; remediation plan approved by the board.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from the Taiwan parent must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered foreign-exchange capital account at a designated bank. The remitter must reference the FDI registration certificate and use the SAFE purpose code for inward direct investment equity capital. After the funds credit, the bank verifies the entry against the FDI foreign-exchange registration and allows conversion to RMB only for use within the negative-list permitted scope. A licensed Chinese certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report before the bank releases funds for operational disbursements; any subsequent capital increase must follow the same SAFE registration and capital-verification cycle.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier settlements and merchant payouts should be executed via SWIFT MT103 using purpose codes that match the underlying service-trade or goods-trade declaration; for larger physical-goods purchases, the WFOE may open Commercial Letters of Credit or use Documentary Collections through the same tier-1 bank to ensure customs and trade documents remain aligned with SAFE verification. Virtual-card spend is cleared by Mastercard or Visa networks; treasury must fund a settlement account at the sponsor bank and reconcile interchange, scheme fees, chargebacks, and merchant payouts. For RMB-denominated cross-border payments, use CIPS with an MT103-equivalent remittance message; TWD and non-RMB currencies are routed via SWIFT to the bank's correspondent network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB forward contracts (e.g., USD/CNY, and TWD/CNY where quoted) offered by a SAFE-licensed designated bank, requiring underlying trade or service exposure and documentary verification.
RMB/USD or RMB/TWD foreign-exchange swaps for cash-flow tenor matching where a genuine current-account exposure exists.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign-currency liabilities or settlement infrastructure investments, subject to SAFE registration and macroprudential capital-flow rules.
Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options and simple risk-reversal combinations permitted for hedging actual foreign-currency receipts or payables, not for speculative trading.

Non-deliverable forwards are not a permissible onshore instrument for the WFOE; NDFs may only be considered by an independent offshore treasury affiliate under its own local licensing, and such positions must not be booked back into the mainland WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Declaration and Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Department of Commercial Services via the MOEA Company Registration Online System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January in each year for the immediately preceding calendar year; any qualifying change in directors, managers, shareholders with 10% or greater equity participation, or ultimate beneficial owners must also be reported within 30 days of the change event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 per violation under Company Act Article 22-1; continued failure after formal correction order can lead to administrative strike-off or deregistration of the company, with personal exposure for responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Annual Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (regional bureau in the WFOE's registered jurisdiction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May through 31 May of the year following the tax year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the final statutory due date is 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 2% per month or fraction thereof on the unpaid tax, capped at 20%, plus monthly interest at the prescribed tax bureau rate; unfiled or underreported returns may attract additional income-tax violation fines and enforced collection measures (asset attachments and tax liens), but the income-tax delinquency does not by itself create a corporate strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Report, and Earnings Distribution Proposal (CPA-audited where the statutory thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders'/Members' Meeting; audited copy filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within the annual declaration and, for licensed financial institutions, with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal-year end, i.e. by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE; FSC-licensed virtual-card issuers must submit audited financial statements to FSC within 3 months after year-end (by 31 March) unless the license imposes a shorter period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers may be subject to administrative fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 under the Company Act for failure to prepare or approve annual financial statements; omission of the mandatory CPA audit renders the annual declaration materially defective and may lead to registration rejection, supervisory sanctions, suspension of the virtual-card license, and eventual administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after each fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies), covering business operation, shareholding, financial condition, and remittance activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in revocation of the foreign-investment approval, an order requiring the foreign investor to dispose of shares, loss of foreign-investment protections and remittance privileges, and repeated non-compliance can be referred to the company registration authority for strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT, Internal Control, and Audited Compliance Report for the Licensed Corporate Virtual Card Issuer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements and compliance report due within 3 months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March); annual AML/CFT self-assessment and internal-control report due by 30 April unless the FSC license imposes an earlier deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FSC may impose correction orders, fines, suspension of card-issuing business, revocation of the statutory license, disqualification of responsible persons, and referral for administrative strike-off in the case of serious or repeated delinquency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the Ministry of Economic Affairs delegated standards for the WFOE when: (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. US$1.0 million); (ii) outstanding financial-institution loans, credits, or guarantees exceed NT$30 million at the balance-sheet date; (iii) the company is a licensed financial institution or card-issuing fintech supervised by the FSC, regardless of capital size; or (iv) the constitutive documents or shareholder resolutions require CPA audit and certification. No separate turnover or headcount threshold applies to a private WFOE under Taiwan company law; public-company consolidation thresholds are governed by the Securities and Exchange Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS) as endorsed by the FSC for public companies and licensed financial institutions; for a non-public WFOE, the statutory books are maintained under the Commercial Accounting Act and Business Entity Accounting Treatment Standards, which are substantially IFRS-aligned, with annual tax-basis reconciliation schedules prepared under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must file any change in directors, managers, shareholders holding 10% or more of equity, or ultimate beneficial owners with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the change; additionally, an annual consolidated UBO declaration covering the preceding calendar year must be filed on or before 31 January. The filing is made electronically through the MOEA company registration system and must identify the reportable persons, shareholding percentages, and ultimate beneficial ownership chain. Failure to comply exposes the company to fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 per offense and, after correction orders, administrative strike-off.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,000 - $18,000 per annual audit, with an upward adjustment for FSC-licensed virtual-card issuers requiring AML/CFT integrated audit procedures
